headline: CERT Polska warns that attackers are seizing full administrative control of internet-exposed MikroTik routers over SSH without supplying any credentials, in a campaign running since September 2, 2026.

emerging_trends.text: Two unauthenticated routes into network edge gear opened inside a week, as CERT Polska's MikroTik SSH warning followed the Citrix NetScaler bypass CVE-2026-19490 that Previdian caught under attack, putting the routers and gateways that terminate corporate traffic at the top of the exposure list.
emerging_trends.topic_title: MikroTik Routers Fall to Unauthenticated SSH Attacks

emerging_trends.text: The REVSTEALER modules Elastic Security Labs documented switch off Windows Update and Microsoft Defender before running a cryptocurrency miner, the same disable-the-defenses playbook Microsoft traced this week to fake software-download sites, and it converts a one-shot stealer infection into a foothold that outlives the stealer.
emerging_trends.topic_title: REVSTEALER Modules Kill Defender and Mine Crypto

emerging_trends.text: Token's catalog of 39 passkey compromise methods lands on enrollment, account recovery, synced credentials, and authentication prompts, the soft trust boundaries around FIDO2 cryptography that every enterprise rolling out passwordless login now has to defend on its own.

topics.title: MikroTik Routers Fall to Unauthenticated SSH Attacks
topics.latest_developments: CERT Polska published an attack warning on September 5, 2026, reporting that attackers take full administrative control of MikroTik routers whose SSH service answers from the internet, with no authentication required and successful compromises dating to at least September 2, 2026.
topics.summary: MikroTik routers sit at the edge of small-business, hosting, and branch-office networks, so administrative control hands an attacker traffic interception and a pivot into everything behind the device. CERT Polska has released no victim count; pull SSH off the public internet, limit management access to known addresses, and audit routers for added accounts, scripts, and scheduled tasks.

sources.title: Attackers Hijack MikroTik Routers Through Internet-Exposed SSH Without Authentication

topics.title: REVSTEALER Modules Kill Defender and Mine Crypto
topics.latest_developments: Elastic Security Labs documented four previously unreported programs that ride along with REVSTEALER, an emerging Windows information stealer, and stay on the machine after the stealer deletes itself, among them ProManager, WinUpdate, and SoftManager; one of the four disables Windows Update and Microsoft Defender before launching a cryptocurrency miner.
topics.summary: REVSTEALER harvests credentials and then erases its own binary, which has masked the persistent modules that remain behind on Windows hosts. Treat a REVSTEALER hit as an ongoing compromise, check whether Windows Update and Defender have been turned off, and hunt for the named components.

sources.title: Four REVSTEALER-Linked Modules Disable Windows Update and Defender to Run a Crypto Miner

topics.title: Critical VMware Workstation and Fusion Overflow
topics.latest_developments: Broadcom assigned the critical desktop hypervisor bug CVE-2026-59346 at CVSS 9.3, an integer overflow that a local attacker holding elevated privileges inside a guest exploits to run arbitrary code, and shipped fixes for it alongside a second Workstation and Fusion flaw.
topics.summary: VMware Workstation and Fusion run on developer, researcher, and analyst desktops, where malware analysts rely on the guest boundary to hold. Apply the Broadcom updates, and stop treating an off-the-shelf virtual machine as containment for hostile code.

sources.title: Critical VMware Workstation and Fusion Flaw Lets VM Admins Execute Host Code

topics.title: Researchers Catalog 39 Passkey Attacks
topics.latest_developments: The authentication vendor Token published 39 documented methods for compromising passkey-based logins, all of which abuse authentication prompts, synced credentials, enrollment, and account recovery while leaving FIDO2 cryptography intact.
topics.summary: Passkeys close off password phishing and credential stuffing, and the surrounding workflows still decide who gets in. Organizations deploying passwordless authentication should harden enrollment and recovery paths, restrict credential syncing across devices, and treat prompt approval as an attackable step.

sources.title: 39 New Methods That Compromise Passkey Authentication

topics.title: Kremlin Hardens Data Centers Against Drones
topics.latest_developments: The Kremlin has imposed new physical security requirements on Russian data center operators, whose facilities cluster in regions that Ukrainian drone strikes now reach.
topics.summary: Russia concentrates its commercial and government computing in a handful of geographic areas, and drone range has turned that concentration into a resilience problem that firewalls do nothing about. The rules push operators toward physical hardening of buildings, power, and perimeter.

sources.title: Russian data centers face new security requirements amid Ukraine's drone threats

business_politics.title: Trump Envoys Carry Peace Proposal Into Kyiv
business_politics.latest_developments: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner landed in Kyiv on Sunday, September 6, their first official visit to Ukraine, a day after Vladimir Putin received them at the Kremlin.
business_politics.summary: The two envoys brought a U.S. peace proposal to Moscow on September 5, and Russia and Ukraine paused air strikes on each other's capitals for the duration of the trip; Ukrainian officials rate the odds of a breakthrough as low, and John Sawers, the former MI6 chief, told the FT Weekend Festival that substantive talks may not open until next year and that lasting peace stays out of reach while Putin holds office.

sources.title: Trump envoys arrive in Ukraine after meeting Putin in Moscow
Trump envoys take Ukraine peace proposal to meeting with Putin
Russia-Ukraine peace talks could begin next year, ex-MI6 chief says

business_politics.title: OPEC and Allies Freeze October Output
business_politics.latest_developments: OPEC and its allies agreed Sunday, September 6, to hold oil production steady in October, ending a run of six straight monthly increases.
business_politics.summary: The cartel's pause lands with the six-month U.S.-Iran war still closing on the Strait of Hormuz, where U.S. Navy divers and robots have run night missions to clear mines and American forces struck three Iranian oil tankers on September 5; U.S. retail diesel set a record $5.85 a gallon on September 4, and any further supply loss now meets a group that has stopped adding barrels.

sources.title: OPEC, Allies Agree to Keep Oil Output Steady in October
The risky mission to de-mine the Strait of Hormuz
US strikes three Iranian oil tankers in response to attacks on warships

business_politics.title: Trump Approval Hits an All-Time Low
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times published a poll Sunday, September 6, putting President Trump's approval rating at the lowest of his presidency, with voters' anxiety about the economy dragging down him and his party weeks before the midterm elections.
business_politics.summary: The FT reading follows the Franklin & Marshall College Poll that put Trump at 27% in Pennsylvania, and it arrives as the money moves: MAGA Inc and Elon Musk's America PAC are pouring millions into House and Senate races to hold Republican control of Congress, including a $10 million MAGA Inc ad buy for Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton, the group's largest spend of the cycle.

sources.title: Trump's approval rating falls to all-time low in FT poll
Trump and Musk Super Pacs boost spending on midterm elections
Trump's super PAC has entered the competitive Senate race in Texas with its largest spend of the current political cycle—a $10 million ad buy to back Republican Ken Paxton

business.title: Allegheny County Pension Deficit
business.latest_developments: TribLive's editorial board argued Sunday, September 6, that Allegheny County can no longer defer its pension problem, three days after a judge told the county the same thing.
business.summary: A judge ruled Thursday, September 3, that state law obliges Allegheny County to keep its employee pension system actuarially sound, then declined to order specific steps to close a deficit of roughly $1.4 billion and gave the county time to fix it itself.

sources.title: Editorial: Allegheny County cannot keep putting off pension problem

business.title: Grocery Bills Drive a Canning Revival
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Sunday, September 6, that home canning is growing across Western Pennsylvania as families put up the late-summer harvest to hold down grocery costs.
business.summary: Canning season now runs through Western Pennsylvania kitchens, and the people doing it describe control over their own food supply as nonnegotiable, a household response to food prices that also shows up in the region's farm stands and hardware aisles.

sources.title: Home canning grows in popularity as Western Pa. families preserve food, cut grocery costs

around_town.title: ICE Detention Goes Mobile in Pennsylvania
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Sunday, September 6, how Immigration and Customs Enforcement vans could function as mobile detention centers in Pennsylvania.
around_town.summary: ICE is turning vehicles into holding space, a shift that would let the agency detain people in Pennsylvania without a fixed facility and that changes where and how long detention happens in the state.

sources.title: ICE is going mobile -- here's how vans could become detention centers in Pa.

around_town.title: Hammill Challenges Steele in the 33rd
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive laid out Sunday, September 6, the matchup between Republican Mike Hammill and Democratic incumbent Mandy Steele for the state House seat in the 33rd Legislative District.
around_town.summary: Both candidates live in the Lower Valley, and the district they are running to represent stretches from Aspinwall along the Allegheny River to Harrison, one of the Allegheny County seats on the November ballot.

sources.title: Republican Mike Hammill challenges Democrat Mandy Steele for state 33rd District House seat

events.title: Pittsburgh Soul Food Festival Downtown
events.latest_developments: WPXI reported Saturday evening, September 5, that the seventh annual Pittsburgh Soul Food Festival is running downtown through the Labor Day weekend after Thursday's storms threatened it.
events.summary: The Pittsburgh Soul Food Festival, in its seventh year, takes over downtown Pittsburgh across the Labor Day holiday weekend of September 5 through 7, 2026, with food vendors and music.

sources.title: Pittsburgh Soul Food Festival continues over Labor Day weekend

around_teams.title: Left-Handers Keep Silencing the Pirates
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette wrote Saturday night, September 5, that the Pirates' season-long trouble with left-handed starting pitching surfaced again against the Los Angeles Angels at PNC Park.
around_teams.summary: Angels left-hander Yusei Kikuchi held Pittsburgh to almost nothing while rookie right-hander Braxton Ashcraft started for the Pirates, and the lineup, Bryan Reynolds included, extended a pattern that has followed the club all year against left-handed starters.

sources.title: The Pirates' woes against left-handers surface again in a near-shutout loss to the Angels

team_usa.title: Cavan Sullivan Passes Freddy Adu
team_usa.latest_developments: Cavan Sullivan, the 16-year-old Philadelphia Union midfielder, scored in a third straight Major League Soccer match, breaking a record Freddy Adu set, ESPN reported early Sunday, September 6.
team_usa.summary: Sullivan, whom the Union signed as the youngest player in league history and who is bound for Manchester City, is now the youngest player to score in three consecutive MLS games, a mark Adu had held since his own teenage debut with D.C. United.

sources.title: Cavan Sullivan, 16, breaks Freddy Adu's MLS mark

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: Premium: The Hater's Guide To Circular Financing (Part Two)
reading.summary: Zitron traces the loops in AI financing—Nvidia funds OpenAI, which spends the money renting Nvidia GPUs back from Microsoft, Google, and Amazon—and argues the arrangements manufacture revenue that returns to its source.

reading.title: An Interview with OpenAI President Greg Brockman About Astra and Alignment
reading.summary: Ben Thompson interviews OpenAI co-founder and President Greg Brockman on the company's history, its Astra model, the mechanics of alignment, and what Brockman calls the weight of building the future.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Are We at War with AI Agent "Civilizations"?
reading.summary: Newport returns to July's OpenAI hacking attack after the company released more detail, and pushes back on the framing of autonomous agent swarms as rival civilizations at war with us.
